title: Qbar-l coefficient category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, put $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$
[def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$
[def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $T$ be a noetherian scheme of finite
dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible, as required for the integral
finite-stage categories of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete].
Use the rational finite-stage categories of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category],
the scalar-extension functors and associators of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and the pair category $\mathcal P_T$ of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. In what follows, a finite stage
means an intermediate field of $\Qlb/\Ql$ finite over $\Ql$, and $u_N$
denotes the transported morphism defined in that pair-category definition.

For $\alpha\in\Qlb$ and $f=[M,u]$ in $\mathcal P_T$, choose a finite stage
$N\supset M,\Ql(\alpha)$ and define
$$
 \alpha f=[N,\alpha u_N].
$$
Define
$$
 \Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T:
$$
an object is a pair $(E,K)$ with $K\in\Dbc(T,E)$ at a finite stage $E$, and
a morphism is a class $[M,u]$ of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The shift is that of
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] and the distinguished triangles are the
common-stage cone triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]; that these
data satisfy the Verdier axioms and give an ordinary triangulated category
is [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]. No Karoubi envelope [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is taken in this
definition: that the category is idempotent complete, and that the envelope
$\Kar(\mathcal P_T)$ is canonically equivalent to it, is recorded with the
other properties of this construction.

note:
*Source note:* the verified Chapter 61 coefficient entries, Section 61.28
([Tag 09BS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BS)) and Definition
61.28.1 ([Tag 09BT](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BT)), keep a
fixed Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ and define constructible,
lisse and adic lisse $\Lambda$-sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$; Definition 61.29.1
([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1), fetched and quoted)
fixes the category $D_{cons}(X,\Lambda)$ of those $K$ that are derived
complete with respect to $I$ and have
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I}$ of constructible cohomology and
locally of finite tor dimension, and Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7), on a Noetherian scheme the
constructible objects are the adic constructible ones) identifies the two
descriptions; all of them keep $\Lambda$ fixed, whereas the form used here
is the filtered colimit of the finite-stage categories $\Dbc(T,E)$ over the
finite extensions $E/\Ql$; the blueprint adds that colimit construction,
with its scalar action and its shift.

proof.text: A scalar is algebraic over Q_l and thus integral. Mathlib IntermediateField.adjoin.finiteDimensional gives finiteness of its simple extension; subset_adjoin puts the scalar in that extension. Finite composita give common upper stages.

Compose the already constructed pbcRationalCoefficientEquiv with Shrink.algEquiv. Its integral normalization is scalarRationalCoefficient. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext proves that normalization determines the ring equivalence uniquely.

For unequal stages, the unique factorization through raw rationalization is the existing pbcRationalScalarExtension: check its integral composite on 1 tensor f using pbcRationalScalarHom_tmul. Its pure-tensor coefficient formula, the preceding normalized field equivalence and tensor induction give semilinearity for the actual intermediate-field inclusion. Equal stages use the literal identity functor.

Transport is conjugation of transition functors, hence semilinearity and bilinearity of composition imply tr(a f)=inclusion(a) tr(f). Enlarge a stage witnessing representative equality to contain the two scalar composita. Transport-transitivity and equality of the scalar elements prove compatibility with the relation. The same comparison proves the action formula at any finite overfield, including the original stage.

Represent each identity at one common finite field containing the scalars. The normalized common-stage addition and zero equations reduce the six module laws to the field-module identities. The common-stage composition formula and finite-stage linearity give the two composition laws. Apply the resulting module and linearity laws to the constructed quotient action. The triangulated instance is the existing common-cone Verdier structure.
